SOS100 Relief for farmers in drought stricken Karoo

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
Ardi Williams founder of MPO- Khayelitsha Cookies which employs 40 previously unemployed women from Khayelitsha was so overwhelmed by the drought at Christmas time that she decided to do something about it. She spent R17 000 of her own money and got Man Truck to deliver Hay bales to drought stricken farmers who are so poor they no longer can feed their animals. But it was a drop in the ocean, hay bales wont provide starving livestock sufficient nutrients so she approached other sponsors like BKB feed producers and Pick and Pay stores. BKB is producing lucerne pellets at cost and Pick and Pay set up water donations points for their patrons. Adri delivered the second truck of Hay bales and water in early February.

Last Week Tygerberg radio got involved an appealed to their listeners, mostly reaching the poor Afrikaans community but also expats across the globe. They raised R2.1 million in a week. Some listeners were pensioners, workers donating their weeks pay and one grandmother who lost her granddaughter last year donated her last R150 because her grandchild loved animals and would have hated them to suffer.



Further information:
Ardi is co-ordinating the drive in conjunction with a Facebook site “Boere in Nood” who have identified the most desperate farmers. BKB feed in Outshoorn are producing the pellets and delivering truckloads of feed to farmers.
Some farmers are so desperate they need the feed immediately and can’t wait for the trucks to arrive or the pellets to be made but they have run out of credit at their local co-operatives. So this week the campaign opened accounts in their names at local farmers co-operatives so they can go into their towns and collect feed.
We will speak to the poor people who donated their money in Cape Town, Adri Williams who is driving the campaign, and follow the truck into the parched hinterland to speak to the desperate farmers. It’s an incredibly inspiring story of what ordinary South Africans are doing in the cities to reach out desperate farmers and animals on the farms.

Press Release:


SOS 100 Karoo Rescue
It’s not often that city-dwellers think of walking a day in farmer’s shoes. Scores of farmers countrywide have been crushed by the current drought, losing livestock, crops and livelihood. What brought pensioners, workers and even children together in a recent drive to raise a remarkable R2.2-million for Karoo farms? Carte Blanche meets the heroes bringing hope to parched areas.


Script:


Script: It all began in early February when one woman’s passion launched a major fundraising drive for drought stricken farmers.
Adri “The project come to light on Christmas day when we had lunch and there I said to my Dad God just dropped it in my heart to fill a truck for farmers and bring it through to them. And dad said I am crazy- absolutely crazy.
Script: Undeterred Adri Williams who is no stranger to making a difference persuaded her colleagues at Khayelitsha Cookies, an NPO which employs 70 previously unemployed woman, to come on board. Manager Eunice Nyobole supported the idea whole heartedly
Eunice ” most people they have got attitude towards the farmers but for me it’s about the person who is need it is not about the colour or the race we are talking about somebody who needs help
Script: Adri’s determination saw Khayelitsha Cookies donate R17 000 for feed and the manager of Man trucks donate and drive the first load of feed to Willerston in the Karoo. But nothing had prepared her for how bad things were.
Adri “we woke up at 6 o’clock with the horses crying for food, and speaking to the farmer he seeing the tears in his eyes saying how do you walk out in the morning and your animals are crying for food you are not in a position to feed them
Link “People who live in cities don’t fully understand the extent to which the drought has taken hold in parts of this country its only when you come into these areas and experience the hardship first hand see grown me cry that you understand fully just what is at stake.
Piet “Last week I decided I can’t feed the sheep anymore there is no more money. Financially this is the worst we have ever had it in this part of the world.
John: Does it break your heart when you see your animals dying
Adri “We realised what these farmers are going through and we realised that the credit has run out
Script: Driven to share her experience when she heard Christian radio station Tygerberg 104FM talking about the drought, Adri called in and challenged listeners to do something
Karien “You are tuned into Tygerberg 104FM and this afternoon its grand to welcome you so the drought really has our farmers on their knees and this afternoon we are just asking our listeners to please pledge whatever they can
Script: The SOS100 fundraising drive by Tygerberg 104FM kicked off
Karien: “You are tuned into Tygerberg 104FM and this afternoon its grand to welcome you so the drought really has our farmers on their knees and this afternoon we are just asking our listeners to please pledge whatever they can

Script: This sheep farming area north of Carnarvon in the Karoo has only had rain in isolated patches. These farmers are a hardy proud bunch who have survived many droughts but Pieter Jacobs says the condition of the veld has never been this poor
Pieter “I have been on the farm for 18 years, we have had a year before but this is the first time we have had three years of poor rain. There is no more food for the animals on a bush like this. Normally this bush would be as big as a soccer ball. It would have green foliage and a yellow flower
Script: The water table is dropping and trees are beginning to die. Normally karoo sheep live wild surviving entirely off the land, but for the last two years the farmers have been forced to feed them. Pieter says it’s a pathetic site seeing his sheep waiting at the feed points
Pieter “After a good rain the sheep can smell that there is food. They get thin walking to find it, because they isn’t a lot of it. They burn more energy looking for food than they take in.
Script: It takes 10 hectares to support one sheep so the farms are vast. Pieter drives 200km a day to feed his sheep, and can only afford to feed them every second day. It’s a fine line, but he hopes it will keep them in good enough condition to produce lambs next season
Pieter “We hope that it will rain on Wednesday but we are now at our end. We’ve already sold some assets to buy feed. We are at a bad point with the farm
Script: On the neighbouring farm Gert and his son Johannes are running out of funds to feed their animals
Gert “The availability of food has become a disaster as well as the cost. The price has risen from about R120 a bag of 50kg up to R200 a bag and then you still have to transport. When you get to the water point and you give them the food supplement they just rush towards the buckets trample the weak and the old ones and you are not experiencing any pleasure anymore
Link: All across the Karoo in this unforgiving environment animals like these are dying right next to waterholes
Gert “You will sometimes find the mother is dead and the lamb is lying against her and you give the lamb a bottle to drink and save the lamb but when you come back into the house you smell the death on your clothes, the stench. It is a merciless situation it’s something you cannot comprehend
John “We have been here two days now Pieter and what is noticeable is that yesterday we looked up to the sky we had quite a bit of cloud around there was the promise of rain and yet one day later you look up and there is nothing there
Pieter “We are just unlucky it’s just like nature is half against us. We are a patch of about 30km that just doesn’t get rain. We feel unlucky, it’s not normal
Links: For the first time ever Pieter has had to put these angora lambs into a fenced off area and feed them 3 times a day the reason for that is that there mothers are so weak from a lack of food that their milk has dried up and they can only really fend for themselves
Pieter “I feel like a failure when I come across a dead animal because we farmers are responsible for the food and water and for the health of our animals so a person is heart sore
Karien: We have raised 1.7 million and it’s not just people in the Cape but from Saudi Arabia, Canada Gauteng
Karien “One of the SMS that is very heart warming is a nearly 66 year old woman and trusting God for SASSA to approve my application for pension so I am donating R50 in anticipation.
Script: In the 21 years of the radio station, Karien Basson has never seen such an overwhelming response from the public
Karien “one specific lady came driving in on her bicycle who came in and said I don’t have much but I just want to give, another man came in off the street and said I can give R1200 , it was people from Mitchels Plein it was women from Khayelitsha it ….it was people from old age homes it was primary schools just challenging each other
Script: The Lubbe family heard Adri’s appeal enroute to school
Wendy “Everyone has heard about it but you don’t know how to help you don’t know what to do I mean you can’t contact a farmer and say can I help you although Adri did so it was a good channel to follow that you know that it is actually going to the people who need it.
Mia Lubbe “I felt very upset because I do love animals and I want to become a vet one day and I felt very upset so I wanted to give some of my money
Neil Lubbe “We gave R150 each one of us our Christmas money and our birthday money
Script: Sonya Nortier runs the kitchen at the Apostolic Faith Mission old age home. They managed to raised R1000 selling boerewors rolls and scones to the old folk
Sonja “Just hearing the cry for help and hearing their stories that touched us.
Pearl “Our donation wasn’t all that big but it was there
Peter “And I gave it with an open heart because if the farmers don’t produce how can we survive in the country.
Script: In just 5 days they raised a whopping 2.2 million rand, pensioners, domestic workers, single mothers donating there last cents
Karien “it was the amazing over flowing heart and a grateful spirit that we can just announce … we are at the point of 2.2 Million rand
Adri “I really trusted for one truck on the road back from Willerston seeing the heart sore that I experienced multiplying it for every truck that miracle truck that is arriving and knowing that we raised enough funds for 17
Pieter “All the farmers in our area have spoken about it and we can’t really believe it. It’s nice that there are people that are sharing in our pain. We farmers like giving, we are hospitable, it difficult for us to receive, but this time it’s lekker
Adri “For me see how people work together and how much has gone on behind the scenes to make that truck a reality that is why with every truck I literally get so emotional because it is a miracle truck
Script: Adri’s managed to get the feed donated at cost from BKB in Outshoorn. MAN trucks provided free transport with the manager giving up his weekends to deliver the feed. And as the drought bites deeper into the farmer’s pockets farm workers are being laid off, so this donation of food from Pick and Pay was extremely welcome
Floris Vermeulen “To see people from the other side of the Karoo recognise our problem and the drought and helping us out like this I am happy for the farmers and it’s a privilege to see this in SA
Carl Möller “For us we haven’t experienced this before that people from the city and it doesn’t matter who it is they opened their hearts they opened their pockets to help us. We farmers don’t know how to say thank you.
Link “The farmers here are under no illusions these donations aren’t going to solve the problem and that is down to mother nature but what this is, is a powerful symbol that there are people out there many of whom live in cities who have sympathy for the farmers and what they are going through
JD Möller “This is probably enough for some farmers for just a day or two literally. It’s more the symbolic about it and I think farmers do feel you are alone in it
Script: JD Moller says if it doesn’t rain hard very soon they are in trouble
JD Möller “I think we will get to a stage where livestock will be really depleted in the country and I think it has already been happening the prices are on the increase because of a lack of supply I think what the farmers are trying to do is just keep the core of the herd alive.
Adri “It is phenomenal how as South Africans that we have actually got it in us to work together for a good cause
JD Möller “People help and people come together and they stick together and I think maybe that is a message for hope out there that um we can stick together
Script: This incredible act of goodwill will give these farmers a sense of comfort but unless real relief comes soon it may be the end for many of them
Pieter “We are the first generation of farmers since 1994 that doesn’t get help from the Government. In times like this you get rid of assets and your last savings. There will be a breaking point when you have to stop farming. Our belief and hope is that it is not going to happen. We don’t want anyone to leave the Karoo, we are all friends, a big family that farms together.

And as the drought bites deeper into the farmer’s pockets farm workers are being laid off, so this donation of food from Pick and Pay was extremely welcome Floris Vermeulen “To see people from the other side of the Karoo recognise our problem and the drought and helping us out like this I am happy for the farmers and it’s a privilege to see this in SA Carl Möller “For us we haven’t experienced this before that people from the city and it doesn’t matter who it is they opened their hearts they opened their pockets to help us. We farmers don’t know how to say thank you. Link “The farmers here are under no illusions these donations aren’t going to solve the problem and that is down to mother nature but what this is, is a powerful symbol that there are people out there many of whom live in cities who have sympathy for the farmers and what they are going through JD Möller “This is probably enough for some farmers for just a day or two literally. It’s more the symbolic about it and I think farmers do feel you are alone in it Script: JD Moller says if it doesn’t rain hard very soon they are in trouble JD Möller “I think we will get to a stage where livestock will be really depleted in the country and I think it has already been happening the prices are on the increase because of a lack of supply I think what the farmers are trying to do is just keep the core of the herd alive. Adri “It is phenomenal how as South Africans that we have actually got it in us to work together for a good cause JD Möller “People help and people come together and they stick together and I think maybe that is a message for hope out there that um we can stick together Script: This incredible act of goodwill will give these farmers a sense of comfort but unless real relief comes soon it may be the end for many of them Pieter “We are the first generation of farmers since 1994 that doesn’t get help from the Government. In times like this you get rid of assets and your last savings. There will be a breaking point when you have to stop farming. Our belief and hope is that it is not going to happen. We don’t want anyone to leave the Karoo, we are all friends, a big family that farms together. metadata.Summary: Ardi Williams founder of MPO- Khayelitsha Cookies which employs 40 previously unemployed women from Khayelitsha was so overwhelmed by the drought at Christmas time that she decided to do something about it. She spent R17 000 of her own money and got Man Truck to deliver Hay bales to drought stricken farmers who are so poor they no longer can feed their animals. But it was a drop in the ocean, hay bales wont provide starving livestock sufficient nutrients so she approached other sponsors like BKB feed producers and Pick and Pay stores. BKB is producing lucerne pellets at cost and Pick and Pay set up water donations points for their patrons. Adri delivered the second truck of Hay bales and water in early February. Last Week Tygerberg radio got involved an appealed to their listeners, mostly reaching the poor Afrikaans community but also expats across the globe. They raised R2.1 million in a week. Some listeners were pensioners, workers donating their weeks pay and one grandmother who lost her granddaughter last year donated her last R150 because her grandchild loved animals and would have hated them to suffer.
metadata.Further information: Ardi is co-ordinating the drive in conjunction with a Facebook site “Boere in Nood” who have identified the most desperate farmers. BKB feed in Outshoorn are producing the pellets and delivering truckloads of feed to farmers. Some farmers are so desperate they need the feed immediately and can’t wait for the trucks to arrive or the pellets to be made but they have run out of credit at their local co-operatives. So this week the campaign opened accounts in their names at local farmers co-operatives so they can go into their towns and collect feed. We will speak to the poor people who donated their money in Cape Town, Adri Williams who is driving the campaign, and follow the truck into the parched hinterland to speak to the desperate farmers. It’s an incredibly inspiring story of what ordinary South Africans are doing in the cities to reach out desperate farmers and animals on the farms.
